title: Exodus Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Exodus chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Exodus Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Exodus Chapter 10.

questions.question: Who did the LORD say went in unto Pharaoh because He had hardened his heart?
questions.correctAnswer: Moses
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:1 states that the LORD said unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh: for I have hardened his heart.

questions.question: What reason did the LORD give for hardening Pharaoh's heart and the heart of his servants?
options: To show His signs before Pharaoh
questions.correctAnswer: To show His signs before Pharaoh
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:1 explains that the heart was hardened so that God might show His signs before Pharaoh.

questions.question: According to Exodus 10:2, to whom was Moses instructed to tell what God had done in Egypt?
options: His son and his son's son
questions.correctAnswer: His son and his son's son
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:2 says Moses should tell in the ears of his son and his son's son what God had wrought in Egypt.

questions.question: What did Moses and Aaron command Pharaoh to do in order for the people to serve the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Let the people go
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:3 states that Moses and Aaron said, Let my people go, that they may serve me.

questions.question: What did the LORD warn Pharaoh would come if he refused to let the people go?
questions.correctAnswer: Locusts
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:4 records the warning that if Pharaoh refused, locusts would come into his coast.

questions.question: How did the locusts affect the land according to the LORD's warning?
options: They covered the face of the earth and ate the remaining crops and trees
questions.correctAnswer: They covered the face of the earth and ate the remaining crops and trees
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:5 states locusts would cover the earth so no one could see it and would eat the residue and every tree.

questions.question: Who said to Pharaoh, 'How long shall this man be a snare unto us?'
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh's servants
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:7 says Pharaoh's servants asked him how long Moses would be a snare unto them.

questions.question: When Pharaoh told Moses and Aaron to go serve the LORD, what question did he ask them?
questions.correctAnswer: Who shall go?
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:8 records Pharaoh asking, But who are they that shall go?

questions.question: What groups of people and animals did Moses say would go with them to serve the LORD?
options: Young, old, sons, daughters, flocks and herds
questions.correctAnswer: Young, old, sons, daughters, flocks and herds
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:9 says Moses replied they will go with their young and old, sons and daughters, flocks and herds.

questions.question: What did Pharaoh say to Moses and Aaron after agreeing to let them go with their little ones?
options: Let the LORD be with you
questions.correctAnswer: Let the LORD be with you
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:10 says Pharaoh said, Let the LORD be so with you, as I will let you go, and your little ones.

questions.question: True or False: The locusts came after Moses stretched out his rod over the land and the LORD sent an east wind.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:13 explains Moses stretched out his rod and the LORD brought an east wind that brought the locusts.

questions.question: True or False: Pharaoh's heart was softened and he immediately let the children of Israel go after the locust plague.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:20 says the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart so he would not let the children of Israel go.

questions.question: True or False: The darkness that covered Egypt lasted for three days and could be felt.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:22 states there was a thick darkness over Egypt for three days which could be felt.

questions.question: True or False: According to Exodus 10, the children of Israel also experienced the darkness over Egypt.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:23 mentions the children of Israel had light in their dwellings during the darkness in Egypt.

questions.question: In Exodus 10, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Moses stretching out his hand for darkness
The LORD telling Moses to go in unto Pharaoh
Pharaoh calling Moses and Aaron in haste
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD telling Moses to go in unto Pharaoh
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:1 is the earliest event where the LORD tells Moses to go in unto Pharaoh, before the other events happen.

medium.title: Exodus Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Exodus Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What command did the LORD give Moses regarding the locusts in Egypt?
options: Stretch out thine hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts to come
Pray for the locusts to leave Egypt
Build a barrier to keep the locusts out
Send the locusts to the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: Stretch out thine hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts to come
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:12 instructs Moses to stretch out his hand over the land of Egypt so that the locusts come upon the land and devour what remains after the hail, demonstrating obedience to God's command.

questions.question: How long did the east wind, which brought the locusts, blow over Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: All day and all night
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:13 states the east wind blew all day and all night, bringing the locusts the next morning, showing God's control over natural elements to fulfill His purposes.

questions.question: What was unique about the locusts that came upon Egypt?
options: There were no such locusts before or after them
They were smaller than usual locusts
questions.correctAnswer: There were no such locusts before or after them
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:14 highlights the grievous nature of these locusts, saying no such locusts had appeared before or would appear again, underscoring the severity of God's judgment.

questions.question: According to Exodus 10, what was the effect of the locusts on the land of Egypt?
options: They covered the earth and ate every herb and remaining fruit
They only ate the herbs near the Nile
They destroyed only the crops in Pharaoh's garden
questions.correctAnswer: They covered the earth and ate every herb and remaining fruit
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:15 describes how the locusts covered the whole earth, darkening the land and consuming all green herbs and fruit left after the hail, showing the completeness of God's judgment.

questions.question: What did Pharaoh confess to Moses and Aaron after the locust plague?
options: I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you
I will never let Israel go
I will increase the Israelites' workload
I do not believe in your God
questions.correctAnswer: I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:16 records Pharaoh's confession acknowledging his sin against God and Moses and Aaron, demonstrating a moment of humility under God's discipline.

questions.question: What did Pharaoh ask Moses to do after confessing his sin?
options: Pray to the LORD to remove the death that was coming
Let him keep the Israelites as slaves
Make another plague come upon Egypt
Allow only the men to leave Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Pray to the LORD to remove the death that was coming
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:17 shows Pharaoh requesting Moses to intercede with God to take away the impending death, highlighting the power of prayer and intercession.

questions.question: How did the LORD respond to Moses' intercession regarding the locusts?
options: He sent a strong west wind to remove the locusts into the Red sea
He allowed the locusts to remain longer
questions.correctAnswer: He sent a strong west wind to remove the locusts into the Red sea
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:19 explains that God sent a mighty west wind to remove the locusts, showing His mercy in response to intercession.

questions.question: What was the spiritual significance of Pharaoh's heart being hardened after the locust plague?
options: It prevented Israel's release despite God's signs
It caused the locusts to return
questions.correctAnswer: It prevented Israel's release despite God's signs
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:20 states that God hardened Pharaoh's heart so he would not let Israel go, emphasizing the theme of divine sovereignty and judgment.

questions.question: What blessing did the children of Israel have during the three days of darkness?
options: They had light in their dwellings while Egypt was dark
They were also covered by darkness
They left Egypt during the darkness
questions.correctAnswer: They had light in their dwellings while Egypt was dark
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:23 contrasts the darkness over Egypt with the light in Israelite homes, symbolizing God's protection and presence with His people.

questions.question: What did Pharaoh allow the Israelites to do after the plague of darkness, and what restriction did he place?
options: Go serve the LORD, but their flocks and herds must stay
Leave Egypt with all their possessions
Stay in Egypt but worship the LORD
Go only with their men, leaving women behind
questions.correctAnswer: Go serve the LORD, but their flocks and herds must stay
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:24 records Pharaoh's concession to let Israelites go but not their livestock, showing partial compliance under pressure.

questions.question: Why did Moses insist that the Israelites take their cattle with them to worship the LORD?
options: Because they needed animals for sacrifices and offerings
Because the cattle could defend them
Because the cattle were a sign of wealth
Because they planned to sell the cattle in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: Because they needed animals for sacrifices and offerings
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:25-26 explain Moses’ reasoning that they must take their cattle because they require them for sacrifices to God, demonstrating faithfulness in worship practices.

questions.question: What was Pharaoh's reaction when Moses insisted on taking the cattle and flocks?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:27 states that the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he refused to let the Israelites go with their cattle, showing continued resistance despite God's signs.

questions.question: According to Exodus 10, what does Pharaoh say will happen if Moses sees his face again?
questions.correctAnswer: He will die
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:28 records Pharaoh warning Moses that seeing his face again will result in death, illustrating Pharaoh's anger and rejection of Moses' demands.

questions.question: How does Moses respond to Pharaoh's threat about seeing his face again?
options: He agrees not to see Pharaoh again
He challenges Pharaoh to a duel
questions.correctAnswer: He agrees not to see Pharaoh again
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:29 shows Moses responding calmly, saying he will not see Pharaoh's face again, reflecting obedience and acceptance of God's plan.

questions.question: What does Exodus 10 teach about the importance of prayer in times of crisis?
options: Pharaoh prayed and God removed the locusts
Prayer was ignored during the plagues
Only Moses prayed, but God did not listen
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh prayed and God removed the locusts
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:17-19 shows Pharaoh's intercession and Moses' prayer leading to God sending a strong wind to remove the locusts, teaching the power of prayer in seeking God's mercy.

hard.title: Exodus Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Exodus Chapter 10.

questions.question: What was the nature of the darkness that covered the land of Egypt in Exodus 10:21-23?
options: A thick darkness which could be felt
A brief shadow lasting a few hours
questions.correctAnswer: A thick darkness which could be felt
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:21 states that the LORD commanded Moses to stretch out his hand toward heaven so that there might be 'darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt.' This indicates a tangible, intense darkness lasting three days as described in verses 22 and 23.

questions.question: For how many days did the thick darkness cover Egypt according to Exodus 10:22?
questions.correctAnswer: Three days
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:22 explicitly states that there was thick darkness in all the land of Egypt for three days after Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven.

questions.question: According to Exodus 10:23, who had light in their dwellings during the darkness?
questions.correctAnswer: All the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:23 states that during the thick darkness, 'all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings,' showing divine protection and separation from the judgment on Egypt.

questions.question: What was Pharaoh's condition for letting the Israelites go as stated in Exodus 10:24?
options: Let them go with all their possessions
Let them go but keep their flocks and herds
Let them go without their children
questions.correctAnswer: Let them go but keep their flocks and herds
questions.explanation: In Exodus 10:24, Pharaoh tells Moses to go serve the LORD but insists that their flocks and herds be stayed behind, though he permits their little ones to go.

questions.question: Why did Moses insist that the Israelites must take their cattle with them, as explained in Exodus 10:26?
options: Because the cattle were valuable trade goods
Because they would sacrifice them to the LORD
Because the cattle were needed for food during travel
questions.correctAnswer: Because they would sacrifice them to the LORD
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:26 explains that Moses said no hoof shall be left behind because the cattle were needed to serve the LORD with sacrifices and burnt offerings, and they did not know with what else to serve until they reached the promised place.

questions.question: What was Pharaoh's response after Moses requested to take sacrifices and burnt offerings in Exodus 10:27?
options: He agreed and let them go
He hardened his heart and refused
He asked for more time to consider
questions.correctAnswer: He hardened his heart and refused
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:27 states that the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and Pharaoh would not let the Israelites go, refusing Moses' request for sacrifices and burnt offerings.

questions.question: What did Pharaoh threaten Moses with in Exodus 10:28 if he saw Pharaoh’s face again?
options: To kill him on that day
questions.correctAnswer: To kill him on that day
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:28 records Pharaoh telling Moses that if he sees Pharaoh's face again on that day, he shall die, showing the severity of Pharaoh's anger and rejection.

questions.question: Moses’ reply to Pharaoh's threat in Exodus 10:29 indicates what about their future encounters?
options: Moses would never return to Egypt
Moses agreed he would not see Pharaoh’s face again
Moses would confront Pharaoh again soon
Moses planned to flee Egypt immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Moses agreed he would not see Pharaoh’s face again
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:29 shows Moses responding that Pharaoh has spoken well and that he will see Pharaoh's face no more, indicating acceptance of the threat and possibly foreshadowing their final confrontation.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God hardening Pharaoh’s heart as described in Exodus 10:20 and 10:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 106:7
questions.explanation: Psalm 106:7 reflects on Israel's history including God hardening Pharaoh’s heart, echoing the theme found in Exodus 10:20 and 10:27, showing continuity in the biblical narrative of divine sovereignty and judgment.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage references the hardening of Pharaoh’s heart as a fulfillment of divine purpose, relating to Exodus 10:1 and 10:20?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 9:17-18
questions.explanation: Romans 9:17-18 discusses God’s sovereign will in hardening Pharaoh’s heart to display His power, directly relating to the theme in Exodus 10:1 and 10:20 of God hardening Pharaoh’s heart for a purpose.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'darkness which may be felt' in Exodus 10:21 is most closely associated with which meaning?
questions.correctAnswer: A thick, palpable darkness
questions.explanation: The Hebrew phrase used in Exodus 10:21 (חֹשֶׁךְ מַשְׁמִיד) denotes a palpable, thick darkness, emphasizing the severity and supernatural nature of the plague that enveloped Egypt.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Exodus 10:21-29 to emphasize the tension between Moses and Pharaoh?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:21-29 uses chiasm, a literary device where ideas are presented and then repeated in reverse order to highlight contrasts and intensify the narrative tension between Moses and Pharaoh.

questions.question: According to Exodus 10:19, how did God remove the locusts from Egypt?
options: By a mighty strong west wind
questions.correctAnswer: By a mighty strong west wind
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:19 states that the LORD turned a mighty strong west wind which took away the locusts and cast them into the Red Sea, showing divine control over nature.

questions.question: True or False: According to Exodus 10:20, after the locust plague, Pharaoh immediately let the Israelites go free.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:20 says that the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart so he would not let the children of Israel go, indicating that Pharaoh did not immediately free them after the locust plague.

questions.question: True or False: In Exodus 10:25, Moses agrees to Pharaoh’s condition to leave flocks and herds behind and not take them out of Egypt.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:25-26 records Moses rejecting Pharaoh’s condition, insisting that their cattle must go with them because they are needed for sacrifices, thus Moses does not agree to leave them behind.

theological.title: Exodus Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Exodus Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God's action in hardening Pharaoh's heart as stated in Exodus 10:1?
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty over human will
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:1 states that the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, demonstrating God's sovereign control over human decisions and history, showing that God's will is ultimately decisive even in human resistance.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about divine revelation is highlighted in Exodus 10:2 where God instructs Moses to tell future generations about His signs?
options: The perpetuity of God's covenant faithfulness
The necessity of human works for salvation
The finality of Old Testament revelation
questions.correctAnswer: The perpetuity of God's covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:2 emphasizes that God's mighty works are to be recounted to future generations, underscoring the ongoing nature of God's covenant faithfulness and His active role in history, which is foundational to biblical theology on revelation and covenant.

questions.question: How does Pharaoh's question in Exodus 10:8 reveal his attitude towards the Israelites and the plague?
options: He doubts the identity and number of the Israelites
He fully submits to God's demands
He acknowledges the power of God immediately
He wants to negotiate terms of release
questions.correctAnswer: He doubts the identity and number of the Israelites
questions.explanation: In Exodus 10:8, Pharaoh asks 'who are they that shall go?' which shows his skepticism and reluctance to accept the Israelites' demand, reflecting human resistance to God's redemptive plan despite evident signs.

questions.question: What does the description of the locust plague in Exodus 10:6 teach about the severity of God's judgment?
options: It is mild and easily bearable
It is symbolic rather than real
questions.correctAnswer: It is unprecedented in history
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:6 describes the locust plague as something never seen by Pharaoh's ancestors, emphasizing the unique and severe nature of God's judgment as a divine act of justice against Egypt.

questions.question: What theological insight about sin and repentance is illustrated by Pharaoh's confession in Exodus 10:16?
options: Recognition of sin is the first step toward forgiveness
Sin has no consequences on the community
questions.correctAnswer: Recognition of sin is the first step toward forgiveness
questions.explanation: Pharaoh's admission 'I have sinned' in Exodus 10:16 shows that acknowledging one's sin is necessary before seeking God's mercy, highlighting a core principle of repentance in biblical theology.

questions.question: According to Exodus 10:20, what does God's continued hardening of Pharaoh's heart demonstrate about His divine plan?
options: God's plan includes the persistence of human obstinacy to fulfill His purposes
God abandons those who resist Him
God's plan is limited by human free will
God desires immediate obedience from all
questions.correctAnswer: God's plan includes the persistence of human obstinacy to fulfill His purposes
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:20 shows that God hardened Pharaoh’s heart so he would not release the Israelites, indicating that God’s sovereign plan can include the use of human stubbornness to accomplish ultimate redemption.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed by the darkness over Egypt for three days as described in Exodus 10:22?
options: God's power over creation and natural order
questions.correctAnswer: God's power over creation and natural order
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:22 describes a darkness that could be felt, a supernatural phenomenon demonstrating God's authority over natural elements, reinforcing His omnipotence as Creator and Judge.

questions.question: How does Exodus 10:23 foreshadow the salvation of the Israelites in the broader redemptive narrative of Scripture?
options: The Israelites had light in their dwellings while Egypt was dark, symbolizing deliverance through God's protection
The Israelites were also afflicted by the darkness
Pharaoh's servants protected the Israelites from the darkness
The darkness was a natural occurrence without spiritual meaning
questions.correctAnswer: The Israelites had light in their dwellings while Egypt was dark, symbolizing deliverance through God's protection
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:23 points to the distinction between God's people and Egypt, prefiguring salvation and divine protection, a theme that runs throughout the biblical narrative culminating in Christ as the Light of the World.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do Exodus 10:5-6 and Exodus 10:15 convey about God's judgment on Egypt?
options: God's judgment is comprehensive, affecting all aspects of life and is unprecedented in severity
God's judgment is symbolic and temporary
God's judgment spares the land and only affects people
God's judgment is limited to Pharaoh alone
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is comprehensive, affecting all aspects of life and is unprecedented in severity
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 describe locusts covering the earth and consuming all vegetation, and verse 15 confirms no green thing remained, illustrating a total and devastating judgment upon Egypt's land and economy as a demonstration of divine justice.

questions.question: What theological significance is found in Moses' insistence in Exodus 10:25-26 that sacrifices and all cattle must go with the Israelites?
options: It shows the necessity of worship and obedience to God in the journey of redemption
It indicates Moses' desire for wealth
It reflects a purely economic concern
It shows that animals were more important than people
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the necessity of worship and obedience to God in the journey of redemption
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:25-26 reveals Moses' concern for proper worship through sacrifices, emphasizing that redemption involves both physical deliverance and covenantal worship, a key doctrine in the relationship between God and His people.

questions.question: How does Exodus 10:13 reveal God's control over natural elements in the execution of His judgment?
options: God brought an east wind to bring the locusts, showing divine orchestration of nature
The east wind was a coincidence without divine intent
The wind was harmful to the Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: God brought an east wind to bring the locusts, showing divine orchestration of nature
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:13 states that the LORD brought an east wind all day and night to bring the locusts, demonstrating God's sovereign control over natural forces to fulfill His purposes of judgment.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Exodus 10:16-17 and Exodus 10:19 reveal about God's justice and mercy?
options: God shows mercy by removing judgment when Pharaoh repents, but also executes justice by sending and removing the plague
God's justice is arbitrary and unrelated to human actions
God is indifferent to human sin
questions.correctAnswer: God shows mercy by removing judgment when Pharaoh repents, but also executes justice by sending and removing the plague
questions.explanation: Pharaoh's confession and plea in verses 16-17 lead God to send a strong west wind to remove the locusts in verse 19, illustrating a balance of divine justice in judgment and mercy in response to repentance.

questions.question: What does the narrative arc of Exodus 10:24-29 demonstrate about Pharaoh's hardened heart and God's redemptive plan?
options: Despite apparent concessions, Pharaoh ultimately refuses to release Israel, underscoring God's sovereignty in redemption
Pharaoh immediately releases Israel with full blessings
Israel chooses to stay in Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Despite apparent concessions, Pharaoh ultimately refuses to release Israel, underscoring God's sovereignty in redemption
questions.explanation: Verses 24-29 show Pharaoh offering limited release but then hardening his heart again, highlighting the persistent human resistance that God sovereignly overcomes in His redemptive purpose for Israel.

questions.question: How does the locust plague in Exodus 10 illustrate the doctrine of God's judgment on sin in a redemptive context?
options: God's judgment is both a warning and a means to bring about deliverance for His people
God's judgment is random and unjust
God's judgment is irrelevant to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is both a warning and a means to bring about deliverance for His people
questions.explanation: The plague of locusts in Exodus 10 serves as a divine judgment against Egypt's oppression while simultaneously leading to the liberation of Israel, demonstrating that God's judgment has a redemptive purpose.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's hardening of Pharaoh's heart in Exodus 10:1-20 contradicts human free will and divine justice. What does Exodus 10:1-20 actually teach about this issue?
options: God sovereignly uses Pharaoh's existing stubbornness to fulfill His just purposes without negating human responsibility
God forces Pharaoh to sin against his will, making him blameless
Pharaoh acts freely without any divine influence
God's justice is arbitrary and unrelated to human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly uses Pharaoh's existing stubbornness to fulfill His just purposes without negating human responsibility
questions.explanation: Exodus 10:1-20 shows that God hardened Pharaoh's heart but also that Pharaoh repeatedly refused to humble himself (v3), indicating that God's sovereign hardening works in concert with Pharaoh's own obstinacy, preserving both divine justice and human responsibility (cf. Rom 9:17-18).
